title: Central Government Schemes for Micro Businesses

scope.note: Each scheme has its own eligibility, activity, financing and implementation conditions.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY)
objective: Provide formal institutional credit to micro businesses
Support business establishment, survival and expansion
Encourage self-employment and employment generation
Bring small businesses into the formal financial system
eligibility: Micro enterprises engaged in eligible manufacturing, trading or service activities
New and existing businesses may be considered
Individuals and eligible business entities
Applicant must satisfy the lending institution's credit requirements

categories.Kishor: Above Rs. 50,000 and up to Rs. 5 lakh
categories.Tarun: Above Rs. 5 lakh and up to Rs. 10 lakh
categories.Tarun Plus: Up to Rs. 20 lakh for eligible borrowers who have successfully repaid an earlier Tarun loan

limitations: It is a loan and not a grant
Loan approval is not automatic
The lender evaluates creditworthiness and repayment capacity
Interest and repayment obligations apply
The amount sanctioned may be lower than the amount requested

schemes.name: CGTMSE
schemes.full_name: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises
objective: Improve access to institutional credit
Reduce the lender's risk
Facilitate lending to eligible MSEs where conventional collateral may be a constraint
eligibility: Eligible Micro and Small Enterprises
New and existing eligible businesses
Credit must be provided through participating/member lending institutions
Business and loan must satisfy applicable CGTMSE conditions

financial_support.description: CGTMSE provides guarantee support to the lender rather than directly giving cash to the entrepreneur.

limitations: CGTMSE does not directly provide the business loan
It does not guarantee that a bank will approve the loan
The borrower remains responsible for repayment
Guarantee coverage and applicable fees depend on current rules
The lender still performs its credit assessment

schemes.name: PMEGP
objective: Create self-employment opportunities
Generate employment through new micro enterprises
Promote entrepreneurship in rural and urban areas
Support establishment of new non-farm micro enterprises
eligibility: Individual applicant must generally be above 18 years
No income ceiling for individual applicants
For projects above Rs. 10 lakh in manufacturing or Rs. 5 lakh in business/service, at least Class 8 qualification is generally required
Primarily intended for new enterprises
Project and applicant must satisfy PMEGP conditions

financial_support.subsidy: Margin-money subsidy generally ranges from 15% to 35%, depending on category and location

limitations: Primarily intended for new units
Existing businesses generally cannot claim a fresh new-unit PMEGP subsidy
Bank finance is required
Applicant contribution is required
Subsidy is subject to project conditions and compliance
Bank appraisal is required
best_for: Starting a new micro manufacturing business
Starting a new eligible service business
New entrepreneurs seeking subsidy-linked bank finance

schemes.name: PMEGP Second Loan / Upgradation Assistance
objective: Support expansion of successful existing micro businesses
Help existing units modernize or upgrade
Increase production and business capacity
Support employment generation through expansion
eligibility: Existing qualifying PMEGP or MUDRA unit
Previous loan must satisfy the prescribed repayment conditions
Unit should generally have been profitable for the required period
Udyam Registration is required
Other PMEGP conditions must be satisfied

financial_support.subsidy: Subject to applicable PMEGP second-loan rules

limitations: Not available to every existing business
Previous qualifying PMEGP/MUDRA financing is important
Repayment and profitability conditions apply
Bank appraisal is required
It is not an unconditional grant
best_for: Businesses that previously received MUDRA finance
Businesses that previously received PMEGP assistance

schemes.name: PM SVANidhi
schemes.full_name: Prime Minister Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi
objective: Provide working capital to street vendors
Reduce dependence on informal lenders
Promote formal credit access
Encourage digital transactions and repayment history
eligibility: Eligible street vendors covered under the scheme
Vendor identification/certification requirements apply
Applicant must satisfy applicable local and scheme conditions

financial_support.description: Successive credit facilities may be available subject to repayment and other scheme conditions.

limitations: Primarily targeted at street vendors
A normal fixed-location grocery shop is generally not the target beneficiary
It is credit rather than a general business grant
Local identification and documentation requirements apply
best_for: Other eligible mobile or street sellers

schemes.name: Stand-Up India
objective: Promote entrepreneurship among women and SC/ST communities
Facilitate bank finance for new enterprises
Encourage creation of greenfield enterprises
Promote employment and economic participation
eligibility: Applicant must generally be at least 18 years old
Applicant must be a woman or SC/ST entrepreneur
Enterprise must generally be a new greenfield enterprise
Applicant must satisfy bank and scheme requirements
Applicant should not be in default to a bank or financial institution

financial_support.loan: Generally Rs. 10 lakh to Rs. 1 crore

limitations: Primarily intended for new greenfield enterprises
Not a general subsidy scheme
Category-specific eligibility applies
Bank credit assessment is required
Loan must be repaid

common_documents: GST registration and returns where applicable
overall_objective: Central Government schemes for micro enterprises aim to improve access to formal finance, reduce credit constraints, encourage entrepreneurship and self-employment, support business expansion and modernization, generate employment and integrate micro businesses into the formal financial ecosystem.
